key_insight: OpenCoF explores a new way for models to reason by generating temporally linked video frames, turning video generation into a step-by-step reasoning process. The paper argues that this Chain-of-Frame (CoF) paradigm can support more reliable reasoning than text-only chain-of-thought in certain tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of dedicated supervision and model design for reasoning through video generation. Existing video generators are trained mostly on general video data, which makes them weak at learning diverse, structured CoF reasoning behaviors.
method: Introduces an OpenCoF framework to study and improve reasoning via video generation.
Uses temporally connected frames as intermediate reasoning steps, rather than only final outputs.
Designs training/evaluation settings that better expose models to CoF-style supervision and reasoning patterns.
impact: This matters for AI practitioners because it expands reasoning beyond text into a multimodal, time-based format that may better capture cause-and-effect and sequential decision making. It could improve how future models plan, explain, and generate evidence-backed outputs in dynamic environments.
visual_elements: A side-by-side diagram comparing Chain-of-Thought text reasoning vs. Chain-of-Frame video reasoning
A frame timeline showing how each generated frame represents a reasoning step
An architecture flowchart for the OpenCoF training/evaluation pipeline
An icon-based comparison of general video generation data vs. CoF-specific supervision
paper_title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
paper_authors: Xinyan Chen, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Dongzhi Jiang, Hongsheng Li
